_comment: Nothing here refuses a selection. `families` are groupId prefixes whose modules must stay together: selecting one jar of a family pulls every jar of that family present in the application into the bundle. The only hard errors are unidentifiable coordinates and two jars holding the same class path with different bytes.

families.org.springframework: Spring Framework, Boot, Security, Data: one release train
families.com.fasterxml.jackson: Jackson core, databind, annotations and modules share one version
families.io.netty: Netty modules share one version and ship platform native libraries
families.org.apache.tomcat: embedded Tomcat core, el and websocket share one version
families.org.apache.logging.log4j: Log4j API, bridges and core share one version
families.ch.qos.logback: Logback classic and core share one version
families.org.slf4j: SLF4J API, providers and bridges must match
families.org.jetbrains.kotlin: Kotlin standard library modules share one version
families.org.jetbrains.kotlinx: Kotlin coroutines / serialization modules share one version
families.org.bouncycastle: BouncyCastle provider, pkix and util share one version
families.com.google.protobuf: protobuf runtime and generated code are version coupled
families.io.jsonwebtoken: jjwt api, impl and jackson share one version

signed_jar_note: its signature is stripped by the merge. A JCE provider such as BouncyCastle then loads on OpenJDK builds (Temurin, Corretto, Zulu) but is rejected by Oracle JDK

equivalence._comment: Non-dependency entries ignored by the application equivalence check (files that always change on a rebuild)
